The flakes fall lightly and dissolve quickly on the palate, and are used as dipping salt or a garnish on finished dishes. Through Japan Industrial Promotion Inc. (JIP Japan), partners in Europe and Southeast Asia are sought for distribution and private-label OEM.

sections.heading: The opportunity
paragraphs: Awayuki is a Japanese finishing salt designed to be seen as well as tasted. Sprinkled over a plated dish, it looks like fine snow and dissolves quickly. This opportunity is for partners in Europe and Southeast Asia who want to distribute the Awayuki range or explore private-label and OEM production built around it.

Awayuki is a culinary product for the kitchen and the table. Its relevant buyers are food companies, restaurants and retailers, not any non-food channel. It is introduced through Japan Industrial Promotion Inc. (JIP Japan).

sections.heading: The manufacturer
paragraphs: Awayuki is made by 日東食品工業株式会社, which uses the English name Nittou Food Industry on its website and sells under the Nittou Relay (ニットーリレー) brand. The company began in April 1937 in Hiroshima as a maker of kelp tea and was incorporated in December 1947. Its head office and main factory are in Hagoromo-cho, Naka-ku, Hiroshima City.

The company is best known for kelp tea made from Rishiri and Rebun island kelp from Hokkaido, and has since broadened into instant powdered drinks, pickling bases, barley tea, soups and other powder-processed foods. Awayuki is one of its product series.

sections.heading: The Awayuki range
paragraphs: The Awayuki series on the official site lists Awayuki salt, Moshio Awayuki salt, Sakura Moshio Awayuki salt, Matcha Moshio Awayuki salt and Awayuki sugar. The plain Awayuki salt is made from rice flour (made in Japan) and salt, comes in a 20 g retail pack with a 13-month shelf life, and lists no allergens among its ingredients per the company. The Moshio version uses a salt made from Seto Inland Sea seawater with seaweed extract, in a 15 g pack.

The company describes the flakes as falling softly like snow and melting on the palate, for use as a dipping salt or as a finishing touch on dishes. Because the product is built on rice flour, partners should treat it as a finishing seasoning with its own texture, not as a drop-in replacement for crystalline sea salt in cooking.

sections.heading: Expansion focus: Europe and Southeast Asia
paragraphs: The target markets are Europe and Southeast Asia. Terms, available territories and which items are supplied for export are discussed after a qualified inquiry. No export volumes, certificates or existing overseas partners are claimed here.

sections.heading: Who the manufacturer is looking for
paragraphs: Suitable partners include premium food distributors, retailers and restaurant suppliers who can present a Japanese finishing salt to chefs and food-aware consumers, and food manufacturers or snack producers who want a distinctive topping or seasoning component.

Private-label programs are also in scope. The company states on its site that it offers OEM production, where it makes products to a customer's specification, and ODM production, where it also proposes and develops the product. It lists small-lot manufacturing from 100 kg and help with package and label design. Whether this applies to Awayuki for overseas programs is to be confirmed.

sections.heading: Considerations before you inquire
paragraphs: Imported salt-based seasonings are subject to food import, labelling and ingredient rules that differ between EU member states and Southeast Asian countries. Partners should check local requirements for composition, language labelling and documentation early. Product specifications for overseas packaging, shelf life and certificates should be requested directly.

sections.heading: Why this opportunity
paragraphs: The product has a clear visual identity, a short ingredient list and a manufacturer with 80-plus years of operation and a stated contract-manufacturing service. For partners who work with Japanese food, it offers a finishing salt that is easy to explain on a plate or on a shelf.

faqs.question: What is Awayuki salt made of?
faqs.answer: According to the official product page, the plain Awayuki salt contains rice flour (made in Japan) and salt. The Moshio version uses a salt made from Seto Inland Sea seawater with seaweed extract.

faqs.question: Who manufactures Awayuki?
faqs.answer: 日東食品工業株式会社, a food manufacturer in Hiroshima, Japan, sold under the Nittou Relay brand. It is a different company from other businesses that use a similar name.

faqs.question: Is Awayuki a culinary product?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is a food seasoning used as a dipping salt or finishing salt on dishes.

faqs.question: Does the manufacturer offer OEM or private label?
faqs.answer: The company states that it offers OEM and ODM contract production, with batches from 100 kg. Whether this is available for Awayuki in overseas programs is confirmed in discussion after a qualified inquiry.

faqs.question: Which regions are sought?
faqs.answer: Europe and Southeast Asia. Territory terms are not fixed here and are discussed after a qualified inquiry.
